q: Material is received in a depot against a purchase order and a Receipt Note is posted, but the supplier bill has not yet been paid. How is Purchase Suspense (P.7120) affected?

options.A: It is debited, because every receipt is debited to Purchase Suspense
options.B: It is credited, because material received is credited to Purchase Suspense before bill payment
options.C: It is not affected until the bill is paid
options.D: It is credited to Sales Suspense instead

e: Purchase Suspense is credit-first: Stock is debited and P.7120 is credited on receipt, before the bill is paid.

q: A supplier is given an advance payment before any material is received. What is the effect on Purchase Suspense (P.7120)?

options.A: It is credited, because Purchase Suspense can never be debited first
options.B: It is credited to Sales Suspense
options.C: It has no effect on any suspense head
options.D: It is debited, as an advance payment is the exception that puts a debit first in Purchase Suspense

e: Other than advance payment, credit comes first in P.7120; an advance legitimately creates a debit first.

q: A purchaser deposits auction money, including EMD held for the sale, but the material has not yet been delivered. Where is the money watched?

options.A: In Sales Suspense (P.7140) as a credit, because money is received first and delivery follows later
options.B: Directly as a reduction of Stores in Stock
options.C: In Purchase Suspense (P.7120) as a debit
options.D: In Stock Adjustment Account as a debit

e: Sales Suspense P.7140 is normally credit: money first, including auction proceeds and EMD, with delivery later.

q: Stock verification shows the priced ledger exceeds the ground stock for an item. How is the shortage brought to account?

options.A: Sales Suspense is debited and Stock is credited
options.B: Stock Adjustment Account is debited and Stores in Stock is credited
options.C: Stores in Stock is debited and Stock Adjustment Account is credited
options.D: The shortage is quietly added to issues with no separate entry

e: A shortage is taken through SAA: SAA Dr and Stock Cr, parked for investigation and sanctioned clearance.

q: Stock verification finds ground stock in excess of the priced ledger for an item. What is the correct booking?

options.A: Stores in Stock is debited and Stock Adjustment Account is credited
options.B: Stock Adjustment Account is debited and Stores in Stock is credited
options.C: Sales Suspense is credited and Stock is debited
options.D: No entry is needed for an excess

e: An excess raises book stock: Stock Dr and SAA Cr through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: Material is issued from a depot to a consuming work against an Issue Note. How does Stores in Stock under PH 71 move?

options.A: It is debited, because issues increase stock
options.B: It is credited, because issued material leaves stock and its cost is charged to the consuming work or final head
options.C: It remains unchanged until the work is completed
options.D: It is debited at the original purchase price of the lot

e: Issues reduce stock and are credited to Stores in Stock, valued at issue price from the priced ledger.

q: After material was received and Purchase Suspense was credited, the supplier bill is passed for payment. How is Purchase Suspense cleared to that extent?

options.B: It is credited again when the bill is passed
options.C: It is debited when the bill is passed for payment
options.D: It is transferred to Sales Suspense

e: P.7120 is debited when bills are passed for payment, chasing the earlier credit on receipt until they meet.

q: Material sold earlier, against money already held in Sales Suspense, is now delivered through a Sale Issue Note. What happens?

options.A: Sales Suspense is credited again and Stock is debited
options.B: Purchase Suspense is credited and Stock is debited
options.C: No entry is needed because money was received earlier
options.D: Sales Suspense is debited by contra and Stores in Stock is credited on delivery

e: On delivery, P.7140 is cleared by a contra debit and the stock value leaves Stores in Stock by credit.

q: At the end of a quarter, a balance remains uncleared in the Stock Adjustment Account. With whose sanction is it cleared?

options.A: With the sanction of the depot storekeeper alone
options.B: It is cleared automatically without any sanction
options.C: With the sanction of the purchaser
options.D: With the sanction of the GM / AGM

e: Uncleared quarter-end SAA balances are cleared with GM/AGM sanction.

q: Depot X transfers stock to Depot Y. How do the two depots record the movement in Stores Suspense?

options.A: Both depots debit Stores in Stock
options.B: Both depots credit Stores in Stock
options.C: Depot X credits Stores in Stock as transfers-out and Depot Y debits Stores in Stock as transfers-in
options.D: Depot X debits and Depot Y credits Stores in Stock

e: Transfers-out reduce the sending depot stock by credit; transfers-in raise the receiving depot stock by debit, by the same value.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Purchase Suspense is P.7120 and is credit-first.
2. Sales Suspense is P.7140 and is normally credit.
3. Stock Adjustment Account takes only credits.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: SAA takes both debit and credit for price and ledger-vs-ground differences, so statement 3 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Material received on a Receipt Note is credited to Purchase Suspense before bill payment.
2. Purchase Suspense is debited when a bill is paid or an advance is given.
3. A credit balance in Purchase Suspense means bills paid but material not received.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 1, 2 and 3
options.D: 2 and 3 only

e: A credit balance means material received but bills unpaid; a debit balance means bills paid or advance given with material awaited.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sales Suspense includes auction proceeds and EMD held for sale, received before delivery.
2. A debit balance in Sales Suspense in correct working indicates delivery beyond the money held.
3. Sales Suspense is normally a debit balance.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 2 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: Sales Suspense is normally credit, money first; statement 3 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Stock Adjustment Account is P.7180, with detailed heads P.7181 to P.7192.
2. SAA absorbs price differences and differences between the ledger and the ground.
3. Uncleared quarter-end SAA balances are cleared with GM/AGM sanction.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: All three statements correctly describe SAA, its detailed heads and its quarter-end clearance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the specimen depot month, opening stock was Rs 1,25,00,000.
2. In the specimen month, issues were Rs 96,00,000.
3. In the specimen month, closing stock was Rs 1,25,00,000.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.B: 1 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 2 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: Closing stock in the specimen month was Rs 1,08,61,000, not the opening figure of Rs 1,25,00,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Issues from stock are valued at issue price.
2. Issues are valued at the original purchase price of that specific lot.
3. A receipt into stock increases the asset and is debited to Stores in Stock.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 2 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: Issues are priced at issue price, not the lot purchase price; receipts debit Stores in Stock.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores Suspense is Plan Head 71.
2. Stores in Stock represents the priced value of material physically held in depots.
3. The closing balance of Stores in Stock represents cash in hand.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: The closing balance is the value of stock in hand, material and not cash, so statement 3 is wrong.

q: What is the detailed head for Purchase Suspense under Stores Suspense (PH 71)?
e: Purchase Suspense is P.7120; Sales Suspense is P.7140 and SAA is P.7180.

q: What is the detailed head for Sales Suspense under Stores Suspense (PH 71)?
e: Sales Suspense is P.7140 and normally carries a credit balance, money first.

q: The Stock Adjustment Account under Stores Suspense is denoted by:

options.A: P.7120, with detailed heads P.7121 to P.7130
options.B: P.7140, with detailed heads P.7141 to P.7150
options.C: P.7200, with detailed heads P.7201 to P.7212
options.D: P.7180, with detailed heads P.7181 to P.7192

e: SAA is P.7180; its detailed heads run from P.7181 to P.7192.

q: Stores Suspense, the value account of stores held in depots, is accounted under:

options.B: Plan Head 73
options.C: Plan Head 51
options.D: Plan Head 71

e: Stores Suspense is PH 71 (7100), under Capital Suspense.

q: What does the closing balance of Stores in Stock under PH 71 represent?

options.B: The total Bid Security held from suppliers
options.C: The priced value of stock still in hand in the depots
options.D: The Stores Budget allotment for the year

e: Closing Balance c/d is the value of stock in hand at priced-ledger value, not cash.

q: In Purchase Suspense (P.7120), the normal sequence, other than for advance payment, is:

options.A: Credit first on receipt of material, debit later when the bill is paid
options.B: Debit first on receipt, credit later on bill payment
options.C: Credit only, with no debit ever
options.D: Debit only, with no credit ever

e: The credit-first rule applies in P.7120: receipt credit precedes bill-payment debit; advance payment is the exception.

q: Uncleared balances in the Stock Adjustment Account at the end of a quarter are cleared with the sanction of:

options.B: GM / AGM
options.C: Purchaser of scrap
options.D: Depot Storekeeper

e: Quarter-end uncleared SAA balances require GM/AGM sanction for clearance.

q: Which account absorbs both price differences and differences between the priced ledger and ground stock?

options.B: Stock Adjustment Account (P.7180)
options.C: Sales Suspense (P.7140)
options.D: Stores Budget statement S.3101

e: By design SAA takes both debit and credit for price differences and ledger-vs-ground differences.

q: In the specimen depot month under PH 71, opening stock is Rs 1,25,00,000 and total receipts into stock are Rs 1,05,56,000. What is the total of the debit side of Stores in Stock?
e: Debit total = opening stock plus all receipts into stock.

q: In the specimen month, purchases received are Rs 82,00,000, workshop-manufactured receipts Rs 14,00,000, transfers-in Rs 9,50,000 and verification surplus Rs 6,000. What is the receipts subtotal?
e: Receipts subtotal is the sum of the four receipt items listed.

q: In the specimen month, total debits are Rs 2,30,56,000 and outgoings before closing balance are Rs 1,21,95,000. What is the closing stock?
e: Closing stock = total debits minus outgoings before closing balance, and the account tallies at Rs 2,30,56,000 a side.

q: In the specimen month, issues are Rs 96,00,000, sales including scrap Rs 18,50,000, transfers-out Rs 7,25,000 and shortages via SAA Rs 20,000. What are total outgoings before closing balance?
e: Outgoings are the sum of issues, sales, transfers-out and shortages.

q: In the micro-example, material of Rs 50,00,000 is received and the bill is later passed for Rs 49,60,000. What balance remains in Purchase Suspense?

options.B: Credit balance of Rs 40,000
options.C: Nil balance
options.D: Credit balance of Rs 49,60,000

e: Receipt credited Rs 50,00,000 and bill debited Rs 49,60,000, leaving a credit balance for the short-supply difference.

q: In the micro-example, stock of Rs 50,00,000 suffers issues of Rs 12,00,000, a shortage of Rs 20,000 and an excess of Rs 6,000 through SAA. What are the final stock and the net SAA balance?

options.A: Final stock Rs 37,74,000 and net SAA debit Rs 14,000
options.B: Final stock Rs 38,00,000 and net SAA debit Rs 26,000
options.C: Final stock Rs 37,86,000 and net SAA debit Rs 14,000
options.D: Final stock Rs 37,86,000 and net SAA credit Rs 14,000

e: After issues stock is Rs 38,00,000; shortage reduces it and excess raises it. SAA nets the shortage debit against the excess credit.

q: Which statement about Stores Suspense sub-accounts is NOT correct?

options.A: Purchase Suspense (P.7120) is credit-first on receipt of material
options.B: Stock Adjustment Account (P.7180) can carry either a debit or a credit balance
options.C: Sales Suspense covers auction proceeds received before delivery
options.D: Sales Suspense (P.7140) is normally a debit balance, because material is delivered before money is received

e: Sales Suspense is normally credit, money first; the statement reversing it is not correct.

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Stores in Stock account under PH 71?

options.A: Receipts into stock are debited to Stores in Stock
options.B: Issues to works are credited to Stores in Stock
options.C: Transfers-in are debited and transfers-out are credited
options.D: Its closing balance represents cash in hand available for purchases

e: The closing balance is the priced value of material in hand, not cash.

q: Which statement about the Stock Adjustment Account is NOT correct?

options.B: SAA absorbs ledger-vs-ground differences found on verification
options.C: Uncleared SAA balances can be cleared by the depot storekeeper without any higher sanction
options.D: SAA detailed heads are P.7181 to P.7192 under P.7180

e: Uncleared quarter-end SAA balances need GM/AGM sanction; they are not cleared by the storekeeper alone.

q:
Assertion (A): Purchase Suspense (P.7120) normally shows a credit balance when material has been received but bills remain unpaid.
Reason (R): On receipt of material, Stock is debited and Purchase Suspense is credited before the bill is paid.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: Both are true, and R correctly explains the credit balance through the credit-first rule.
